chunks.title: FireChronicle harmonization method
chunks.text:
[FireChronicle harmonization method | What FireChronicle is]
FireChronicle is a web app that turns NASA FIRMS active-fire detections from MODIS (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) into one consistent monthly burning-activity record for Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan), from November 2000 to the latest available day. The unit is "MODIS-equivalent active fire detections".

chunks.title: FireChronicle harmonization method
chunks.text:
[FireChronicle harmonization method | Why harmonization is needed]
MODIS pixels are about 1 km at nadir; VIIRS I-band pixels are 375 m, so VIIRS detects smaller fires and reports more detections for the same fire. Across Central Asia VIIRS reports about 3.5 times as many detections as MODIS overall, and 2 to 15 times by country and month. Stitching MODIS (before 2012) to VIIRS (after 2012) without calibration creates a false jump.

chunks.title: FireChronicle harmonization method
chunks.text:
[FireChronicle harmonization method | Cleaning]
Only vegetation fires are kept (FIRMS type 0). MODIS detections need confidence of at least 30; VIIRS detections need confidence nominal (n) or high (h). Persistent static sources such as gas flares and industry are removed with a mask of small H3 cells (resolution 8) where most standard-processing detections are flagged as non-vegetation.

chunks.title: FireChronicle harmonization method
chunks.text:
[FireChronicle harmonization method | Grid]
Detections are counted per H3 cell at resolution 5 (about 253 square kilometres) and per month, separately for each sensor.

chunks.title: FireChronicle harmonization method
chunks.text:
[FireChronicle harmonization method | Calibration]
Every VIIRS satellite overlaps MODIS in time, so each one is calibrated directly against MODIS Terra+Aqua. For each stratum (country by calendar month) the ratio k is the sum of VIIRS detections divided by the sum of MODIS detections over overlapping science-quality (standard processing) years, shrunk toward the overall ratio when a stratum has few detections. A yearly drift term in the ratio is fitted because Terra and Aqua orbits are drifting. Calibration never uses provisional near-real-time (NRT) data.

chunks.title: FireChronicle harmonization method
chunks.text:
[FireChronicle harmonization method | Harmonized value]
For each cell and month the harmonized value is the pooled minimum-variance estimate (M + sum of V) / (w_MODIS + sum of k), where M is the MODIS count, V the VIIRS counts and each weight is scaled by how much of the month that sensor observed. Before Aqua started (July 2002) only Terra observed, and its weight is its share of the Terra+Aqua total. When a satellite stops delivering data its weight becomes zero, so the record continues on the remaining satellites in the same units.

chunks.title: FireChronicle harmonization method
chunks.text:
[FireChronicle harmonization method | Uncertainty]
The approximate 90% band combines calibration uncertainty (bootstrap over calibration years, the drift term and the year-level calibration error) with Poisson counting noise.

chunks.title: Satellites and coverage dates
chunks.text:
[Satellites and coverage dates | Coverage dates in NASA FIRMS]
MODIS Collection 6.1: 1 November 2000 to present.
VIIRS Suomi NPP (S-NPP) 375 m: 20 January 2012 to 2 November 2026.
VIIRS NOAA-20 375 m: 1 April 2018 to present.
VIIRS NOAA-21 375 m: 1 March 2023 to present.

chunks.title: Satellites and coverage dates
chunks.text:
[Satellites and coverage dates | Suomi NPP end]
Delivery of new science data from the Suomi NPP satellite ceased at 13:00 UTC on 2 November 2026, as announced by NOAA NESDIS and NASA Earthdata. Historical Suomi NPP data remain available. NASA FIRMS recommends NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 VIIRS as replacements: they carry an identical VIIRS sensor with the same 375 m resolution and fly in the same orbital plane as Suomi NPP, about 50 minutes apart.

chunks.title: Satellites and coverage dates
chunks.text:
[Satellites and coverage dates | MODIS end of life]
NASA Earthdata states that in late 2026 or early 2027 the Terra and Aqua platforms that carry MODIS will begin shutting down operations, and that both platforms are drifting out of their designed orbits, which affects crossing times.

chunks.title: Satellites and coverage dates
chunks.text:
[Satellites and coverage dates | Overpass times]
MODIS on Terra provides the only morning overpass, about 3 hours before Aqua. MODIS on Aqua has an afternoon overpass similar to Suomi NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21.

chunks.title: Satellites and coverage dates
chunks.text:
[Satellites and coverage dates | Product identifiers and DOIs]
MODIS active fire locations distributed by FIRMS: MCD14ML, DOI 10.5067/FIRMS/MODIS/MCD14ML. The near-real-time MODIS product is MCD14DL.
MODIS Terra thermal anomalies Level 2: MOD14 (Aqua: MYD14), Collection 6.1, DOI 10.5067/MODIS/MOD14.061.
VIIRS 375 m active fire, Suomi NPP: VNP14IMG version 2, DOI 10.5067/VIIRS/VNP14IMG.002.
VIIRS 375 m active fire, NOAA-20: VJ114IMG version 2, DOI 10.5067/VIIRS/VJ114IMG.002.
VIIRS 375 m active fire, NOAA-21: VJ214IMG version 2, DOI 10.5067/VIIRS/VJ214IMG.002.

chunks.title: NASA FIRMS data: processing levels and fields
chunks.text:
[NASA FIRMS data: processing levels and fields | Standard vs near-real-time data]
Standard (science-quality) data deliver an internally consistent, well-calibrated record designed for long-term research. FIRMS distributes them as monthly "ML" files, usually available with a 2-3 month lag; the FIRMS archive page mentions about a 5 month lag before NRT data are replaced. Ultra Real-Time (URT), Real-Time (RT) and Near Real-Time (NRT) data are produced faster for emergency response using modified processing. In FireChronicle, months that still contain NRT data are marked provisional.

chunks.title: NASA FIRMS data: processing levels and fields
chunks.text:
[NASA FIRMS data: processing levels and fields | Geolocation of NRT data]
Most of the time the extra location error of MODIS and VIIRS NRT detections is very small (under 100 metres). After spacecraft maneuvers or severe space weather, NRT positioning errors can reach several kilometres; for MODIS Aqua the degraded period can last up to 12 hours.

chunks.title: NASA FIRMS data: processing levels and fields
chunks.text:
[NASA FIRMS data: processing levels and fields | Fields]
latitude, longitude: centre of the detection pixel. acq_date, acq_time: acquisition date and time in UTC. satellite: Terra, Aqua (MODIS) or N (Suomi NPP), N20 (NOAA-20), N21 (NOAA-21). confidence: MODIS 0-100; VIIRS low (l), nominal (n), high (h). frp: fire radiative power in megawatts. daynight: D or N. type (standard processing only): 0 presumed vegetation fire, 1 active volcano, 2 other static land source, 3 offshore. version: collection and processing level, for example 6.1 for MODIS standard processing and 6.1NRT for near-real-time.

chunks.title: NASA FIRMS data: processing levels and fields
chunks.text:
[NASA FIRMS data: processing levels and fields | Access]
FIRMS archive downloads (CSV, SHP, JSON) need Earthdata login or an email code. Country yearly summaries are downloadable as CSV. The FIRMS Area API needs a free MAP_KEY and allows 5000 transactions per 10 minutes.

chunks.title: How to use FireChronicle
chunks.text:
[How to use FireChronicle | Choosing an area]
Pick a country or "Central Asia" from the Area list, draw a polygon on the map (click points, double-click to finish), or enter latitude, longitude and a radius in kilometres. An area is the set of H3 cells whose centres fall inside it.

chunks.title: How to use FireChronicle
chunks.text:
[How to use FireChronicle | Burning activity calendar]
Rows are years, columns are months. Brighter colour means more harmonized fire detections. Hatched cells are provisional (near-real-time data). Modes: Harmonized, Raw MODIS, Raw VIIRS, Naive splice, and Swipe compare, which shows the naive splice and the harmonized record side by side.

chunks.title: How to use FireChronicle
chunks.text:
[How to use FireChronicle | This month vs history]
Compares the current month so far with the same days of the same month in every past year, and reports the percentile and the change against the median.

chunks.title: How to use FireChronicle
chunks.text:
[How to use FireChronicle | High-activity months ahead]
For each of the next 12 calendar months, the share of the last 10 years in which that month was above the area's recent 75th percentile, Laplace-smoothed. Months at 50% or more are marked high-activity. This is climatology, not a forecast.

chunks.title: How to use FireChronicle
chunks.text:
[How to use FireChronicle | Anomaly now]
A map mode that colours each cell by the percentile of the latest complete month against that cell's own history for the same calendar month. Cells with fewer than 5 years of history are grey.

chunks.title: How to use FireChronicle
chunks.text:
[How to use FireChronicle | Downloads]
Hotspot CSV for the selected area and years, monthly series CSV, harmonized dataset CSV for all regions, chart PNGs, and a briefing card PNG. The Cite button copies a citation.

chunks.title: Limitations
chunks.text:
[Limitations | What a hotspot is not]
An active fire detection (hotspot) marks a pixel containing at least one fire at the moment of the satellite overpass. A detection count is not burned area and not fire size. Several detections can come from one large fire, and a small or short fire between overpasses can be missed.

chunks.title: Limitations
chunks.section: Things that hide or distort fires
chunks.text:
[Limitations | Things that hide or distort fires]
Clouds and thick smoke can hide fires. Near-real-time months are provisional and are replaced when science-quality data arrive. Terra and Aqua orbits are drifting, which changes their overpass times. Suomi NPP stopped on 2 November 2026. Calibration ratios are fitted on 2012-2025 and held at their 2025 level for later years.

chunks.title: Limitations
chunks.text:
[Limitations | Not a forecast]
High-activity months are historical climatology. FireChronicle does not predict where or when a specific fire will start.

chunks.title: Limitations
chunks.text:
[Limitations | Not an official product]
FireChronicle uses NASA FIRMS data but is not an official NASA product and is not endorsed by NASA.

chunks.title: FireChronicle validation results
chunks.text:
[FireChronicle validation results | Cross-validation]
Cross-validation of Suomi NPP against its prediction from MODIS (country-month, years 2012-2025): r2 0.988, bias -0.06 percent, mean absolute error 46.95 detections, n = 995.
Cross-validation of NOAA-20 against its prediction from MODIS (country-month, years 2018-2025): r2 0.976, bias 0.53 percent, mean absolute error 45.73 detections, n = 557.
Cross-validation of NOAA-21 against its prediction from MODIS (country-month, years 2023-2025): r2 0.986, bias 1.63 percent, mean absolute error 29.98 detections, n = 203.

chunks.title: FireChronicle validation results
chunks.text:
[FireChronicle validation results | Naive splice vs harmonized jump]
The naive MODIS-to-VIIRS splice shows a jump ratio of 1.7 at the 2012 change point (2012-03), Pettitt test p = 1.3e-14.
The harmonized record shows a jump ratio of 0.46 at change point 2011-01, Pettitt test p = 3.7e-10.
The MODIS-only reference shows a jump ratio of 0.49 at change point 2011-01.

chunks.title: FireChronicle validation results
chunks.text:
[FireChronicle validation results | Calibration ratios and chain check]
Chain check for NOAA-20: the ratio calibrated directly against MODIS is 3.983, via Suomi NPP it is 3.708.

chunks.text:

chunks.title: FireChronicle validation results
chunks.text:
[FireChronicle validation results | Cleaning, refresh and data coverage]
Detections removed because FIRMS type is not 0 (not presumed vegetation fire): 2.9 percent.
Near-real-time detections removed by cleaning: 33.7 percent.
The data refresh cadence is daily at 03:00 UTC, with automatic updates until 2027-05-15.
Data through 2026-11-14.

chunks.title: Fire activity by country (computed from FireChronicle data)
chunks.text:
[Fire activity by country (computed from FireChronicle data) | Central Asia (central-asia)]
Typical fire season in Central Asia: Mar–May and Jul–Oct (months whose median monthly total, over all complete months since November 2000, is at least 8 percent of the sum of monthly medians). The peak month is April.
Median annual harmonized total in Central Asia for 2001-2025: 41 086 MODIS-equivalent detections. The three highest years were 2002 (113 238), 2003 (102 471), 2004 (96 393). The lowest year was 2024 (8 128). The year with the most detections was 2002.
The most active calendar month in Central Asia over the last 10 complete years (2016-2025) is April.
Harmonized detections in 2025 in Central Asia: 18 312 MODIS-equivalent detections, which is 55 percent below the 2001-2025 median.
Mean annual harmonized total in Central Asia: 71 124 in 2001-2011 and 32 992 in 2012-2025, a change of -54 percent (lower in the later period).
Current partial month in Central Asia (November 2026, days 1-14): 403 MODIS-equivalent detections, which is 5 percent above the median of the same days in past years (385). This month is provisional.
Data through 2026-11-14.
